runners_data.name: Jalila Moriviere
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins' string is in excellent form (8/37 in 14 days) and Simon Torrens takes the ride; two recent second-place finishes on Good ground over 20f and 16f indicate it handles conditions perfectly and Jalila Moriviere's prominent style slots naturally into this race shape without redistribution.
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in her last two starts, Jalila Moriviere arrives here in fine recent form, and has run over today's trip and going before. Winless in her last five starts, but carrying 161 lb she shaped with plenty of promise and the conditions look tailored to her strengths.

runners_data.name: Ballybawn Belter
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden makes the trip for Liz Doyle, whose sole runner in the 14-day window gives little trainer form angle; 118 days off is a significant freshness concern and a record showing predominantly soft-ground form (three runs on Soft or Heavy) makes the Good surface a mild query despite an official 154lbs mark.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out is the positive to hold onto, but Ballybawn Belter hasn't won in her last four starts and returns after 118 days off carrying 154 lb. She has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 131 suggests she's competitive at this level.

runners_data.name: Littlefoot
runners_data.note: Won twice over 20f on Good ground and carries the visor; fresh off a 21-day break and trainer Molloy's 0/6 14-day run gives little confidence from the yard but the horse's own form figures on similar going (1W4P from 10 runs) are strong and Sam Ewing partners.
runners_data.comment: Littlefoot showed his best when winning two starts back, but a pulled-up effort last time out is the obvious concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and 21 days gives fair prep time, though carrying 154 lb tests his stamina.

runners_data.name: Intense Approach
runners_data.note: Blinkers applied for John McConnell who is 0/26 in the past fortnight; the form string shows erratic figures including unseating and a pull-up, and the step back to 21f from longer trips may suit, though four Good-ground wins from five sim-going starts is an encouraging underlying stat despite the inconsistency.
runners_data.comment: Intense Approach won five starts back but has since failed to recapture that form, with an unplaced effort last time out among three consecutive poor returns; experience over today's trip and distance is a plus, though a struggling trainer (0/22) and 153 lb are tough asks.

runners_data.name: Kings Hill
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes the mount for Paul Gilligan on an OR-127 horse that finished second most recently on Soft, third on Soft, and won on Heavy — the Good ground is the softest surface in its flat-track record, making conditions a mild concern despite a recent run just 11 days ago.
runners_data.comment: Kings Hill brings solid recent form — a winner three starts back, third two starts back, and runner-up last time out — and has run over today's trip and going before, but 153 lb is a stiff burden and an eighth-of-22 ranking suggests he faces stiffer opposition here.

runners_data.name: Yoradreamer
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained with Danny Mullins aboard, but a recent pulled-up and brought-to-halt on Good ground is a worrying pair of recent figures; the one genuine Good-ground form win came at 25f and the 26f trip here fits the profile, though 0W2P from eight similar-going starts is modest.
runners_data.comment: Yoradreamer was second one start back from a pulled-up latest, but has shown ability, including a win four starts back; he has run over today's trip and going, though ranked 13 of 22 on our rating, he faces a stern test under 153 lb.

runners_data.name: Moonovercloon
runners_data.note: Michael Kenneally takes the 5lb claim for Declan Queally; a visor applied and 13 from 15 runs on Good ground confirms the hold-up horse handles conditions well, but form figures of 8-6-4-7-10 in five consecutive runs on Good are consistently mid-pack without threatening, and a 46-day absence is noted.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 14th of 22 in the field, Moonovercloon has experience of today's trip and going but a return of unplaced, seventh and fourth in recent outings offers limited encouragement, and 152 lb is a stiff burden after 46 days off.

runners_data.name: A Penny A Hundred
runners_data.note: Brian Hayes partners this Mullins-trained hold-up horse that has a solitary win from 15 similar-going starts; a recent seventh on Soft and progressive trip distances up to 28f suggest it needs extreme stamina tests to be seen at best, and the honest but not gruelling pace here may not suit a true stay-all-day profile.

runners_data.name: Shanbally Kid
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy rides for Gordon Elliott (4/37 14-day) but the ⚠ fade flag is significant — this horse is tagged as a hold-up type that fades in the finish, and recent pulled-up and unseat figures over marathon trips on Good underline the concern; a 21-day turnaround at least gives freshness.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and has pulled up twice and unseated in that sequence, Shanbally Kid arrives on a going he has encountered before and 21 days fresh, but his jumping reliability is a serious concern that outweighs his 131 rating.

runners_data.name: Rising Dust
runners_data.note: Six wins from nine prominent-style runs on Good ground is an outstanding stat for this Emmet Mullins-trained eight-year-old; Donagh Meyler takes the ride and an OR of 124 at 150lbs is still competitive — form of 1-1-1 in the three most recent sim-going wins makes this a standout profile for the dominant race shape.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five starts give Rising Dust some profile, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but back-to-back eighths in his most recent outings make him very hard to fancy, and our figures rank him last of the 22 runners here.

runners_data.name: Where's My Jet
runners_data.note: Paul Townend is an undeniable booking for Mullins but the form is deeply uninspiring — five blanks including a pulled-up on Good, and 15th and 10th over similar trips; the style is prominent but the underlying ability suggests this is a yard runner unlikely to threaten the market movers.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up two runs back, Where's My Jet arrives on 53 days off carrying 150 lb, which is a stiff ask; he has run over today's going before, though, and a rating of 129 suggests some residual ability to exploit.

runners_data.name: A Law Of Her Own
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins saddles this nine-year-old mare returning from 289 days off — the longest layoff in the field and a significant concern; her true style is prominent racing and she is a genuine Good-ground operator (14/15 runs on similar going), but the redistribution to midfield and the extended absence combine to make this a watch-and-see runner rather than a confident selection.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 289 days is the chief concern here, and she ranks near the foot of our assessments in this field; that weight of 149 lb adds further pressure. She has run over today's going before, and a win last time out at least brings some recent winning form to the table.

runners_data.name: Baltic Bird
runners_data.note: Ran just 13 days ago for William Durkan, which at least provides recency; a natural prominent racer whose position is constrained by the crowded front ranks — all five recent runs have been on Good ground (15/15), confirming the surface suits, but form figures of 8-6-3-7-3 show consistent mid-group finishes without winning.
runners_data.comment: Baltic Bird has been winless in his last five starts, though a third three starts back offers some encouragement; his two most recent efforts — eighth and sixth — suggest he's struggling to recapture that form, and 149 lb is no help.

runners_data.name: Donnie Devito
runners_data.note: Shane Markey (7lb claim) partners this Ross O'Sullivan-trained seven-year-old whose form reads 3-3-2-3-3 — relentlessly placed but yet to win; a natural front-tracking type whose chances depend partly on reclaiming prominent ground in a crowded field, and the consistent place figures on Good suggest it will be competitive if it secures its position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 18th of 22 on our figures, Donnie Devito faces a stiff ask here; he has been consistently placed in recent starts, though, and has run over today's trip and going before, with 28 days between runs suggesting he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Hermino AA
runners_data.note: Tom Kelly (7lb claim) partners this E McNamara nine-year-old who wore blinkers and won most recently on Soft over 25f; Good ground appears workable (6/15 similar runs) but the form is patchy and the redistribution to midfield reflects a true prominent profile squeezed out — the recent win gives confidence in fitness.
runners_data.comment: Hermino AA was a winner last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, giving him every reason to strip fit off a 53-day break — the main concern is whether the 148 lb burden blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Warriors Wood
runners_data.note: Kevin Healy (7lb claim) rides this young six-year-old for Andrew McNamara who has 1/5 in 14 days; a progressive profile (wins at 20f on Good, second at 20f) and three wins from 10 Good-ground runs stand out for a horse only lightly raced — the prominent style is its natural home but the midfield redistribution limits positional advantage.
runners_data.comment: Warriors Wood has finished fourth and third in his last two starts, with his sole recent win coming three starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before, and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround, but ranked 16 of 22 on our figures, he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Antrim Coast
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe gives this De Bromhead runner (6/42 14-day) a high-profile ride; form figures of 2-2-2-5-6 show a horse that consistently tracks the pace and finishes second, making it a natural beneficiary of prominent racing — the mapping to midfield is the key tactical obstacle in a race this size.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Antrim Coast has been runner-up three times in that sequence — most recently a second three starts back — but back-to-back defeats in sixth and fifth suggest a dip in form; he has run over today's trip and going, though 147 lb is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Rexem
runners_data.note: Josh Williamson (5lb claim) rides for John McConnell who is 0/26 recently; ran just seven days ago and form shows a consistent hold-up profile with a second from five Good-ground runs at 20f — the patience shown in race riding suits a shape where the pace eventually relents, and the short turnaround is worth monitoring for freshness.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 17th of 22 on our figures, Rexem faces a stiff task here, with his trainer yet to land a winner in 22 attempts over the last fortnight; experience over today's trip and going, plus a second last time out, are the only crumbs of comfort.

runners_data.name: Charlie Luciano
runners_data.note: Conor Stone-Walsh partners this Noel Meade-trained seven-year-old (3/13 14-day) who won at Galway over 26f on Good most recently — a direct course-and-distance form tick; hold-up style suits a scenario where the pace collapses late, and Good ground suits (14/15 similar-going starts).
runners_data.comment: Two pulled-ups in recent starts make him hard to trust despite a last-time-out win, and he ranks 19th of 22 on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going before, but 145 lb adds another obstacle.

runners_data.name: Lord Lariat
runners_data.note: 11-year-old for Dermot McLoughlin returning after 90 days; form figures of P-F-8-0 in recent runs are deeply discouraging and the trip of 32f on the last run suggests connections are fishing for extreme stamina, while Good ground and a competitive field make this a very difficult prospect.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five and pulled up most recently, Lord Lariat does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and our rating of 132 suggests he retains more ability than his official mark of 119 implies — the concern is a stop-start recent record that makes him hard to trust.

runners_data.name: El Champo
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell sends out this eight-year-old (2/31 14-day) with a pace hood applied
runners_data.comment: Two pulled-ups in recent starts make El Champo hard to fancy, and he's winless in his last five, ranked 21 of 22 on our figures; a return after 54 days adds to the queries, though he has run over today's trip and going, and a third five starts back offers a distant crumb of comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Addragoole is the confirmed pace-setter and, with no genuine challenger pressing from the front, should dictate an honest but manageable gallop over the 2m6½f trip on Good ground — a sustainable tempo rather than a searching test. Several horses labelled prominent in style (Donnie Devito, Baltic Bird, A Law Of Her Own, Hermino AA, Warriors Wood, Antrim Coast, El Champo) cannot all secure their natural tracking positions in a 22-runner field and have been redistributed to midfield on the map; of these, Donnie Devito's relentless place-form at good pace and Antrim Coast's repeated runner-up finishes suggest they are most likely to hustle forward and actually claim prominent ground. With one steady leader and a compressed midfield pack, the race will be run at a gallop that suits resolute, prominent-to-midfield types who can travel smoothly through traffic and produce a sustained jump-by-jump effort from three out rather than a sudden late burst. The dominant profile is the patient prominent racer — one who sits three to five off the pace, avoids the midfield scrimmage, and can quicken smoothly off a genuine but not brutal tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady pace, prominent wins
scenarios.trigger: If Addragoole controls a measured gallop and the field settles compactly behind, allowing a well-placed prominent racer to stalk and strike.
scenarios.body: Addragoole sets a sensible clip over the stiff Galway 2m6½f track and the runners compress into a tight pack from halfway; horses that travel prominently in third to sixth have first run at the final two fences and the run-in is too short for true hold-up types to reel them in. Jalila Moriviere, Littlefoot and Rising Dust all carry strong form credentials, good trainer/jockey combinations and suit this controlled-but-honest tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, hold-up pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate early gallop causes the field to bunch and stall turning in, freeing a patient hold-up horse to pick up powerfully from the rear.
scenarios.body: A steady pace on Good ground creates a falsely run race where stamina is not truly examined; late runners who have been held off the pace throughout find themselves with genuine momentum at the last while the prominent pack has used itself up jostling for position in the straight. Charlie Luciano (recent Galway form, hold-up profile) and Rexem (consistent place-form on this ground, patient style) are well suited if the closer's late run is enough.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent pack scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple redistributed prominent types succeed in pushing forward and inject friction behind the leader, creating a gruelling mid-race test.
scenarios.body: Donnie Devito, Baltic Bird and Antrim Coast all attempt to access their natural tracking positions, compressing the early pace and raising the tempo from the back of the second mile; the resultant stamina test exposes those who travelled kindly in behind and rewards the horse with the best jumping accuracy and class at the weights. Warriors Wood (young, improving, good-ground specialist) and Donnie Devito (relentless place-form) could profit if the bunching suits their forward thrust.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-runner steals race
scenarios.trigger: If Addragoole is given a completely uncontested lead and the field underestimates its front-running ability, allowing it to slip the field at a crucial point.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing to challenge Addragoole for the lead and a 22-runner pack creating traffic chaos in behind, the front-runner can coast into the straight with a substantial advantage that proves impossible to close on a flat Good surface with limited run-in. Addragoole's historical win at 17f Good and reasonable jumping give it a realistic chance of converting if the field dawdles behind.

races.name: Guinness Handicap

runners_data.name: Shaool
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator trained by JP Murtagh who has won twice at 10f on Good and arrives 31 days fresh; needs the pace to lift turning in but the compact Galway straight can favour late finishers if the race is truly run.|
runners_data.comment: Shaool has back-to-back wins in her recent form and she has run over today's trip and going before, with our rating putting her at the head of this field — but three consecutive poor runs since those victories make it hard to know which version turns up today.

runners_data.name: This Songisforyou
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner here, likely to stride clear unchallenged and control every fraction; STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) reflects it races here outside its typical role but the absence of pace opposition is a notable compensating factor for Emmet Mullins's eight-year-old.|
runners_data.comment: Ran a fine second last time out and returns after just over a month looking primed for this trip and going, This Songisforyou carries 140 lb yet remains winless in recent starts — though that placed effort hints he's close to landing one.

runners_data.name: Dawn Rising
runners_data.note: Declan McDonogh partners this nine-year-old for Joseph O'Brien, placed twice at this trip on Good but the 8/12f last run in a field of this depth is a concern; tracks pace without always producing the decisive turn of foot.|
runners_data.comment: Dawn Rising has experience over today's trip and going, and that second in his last five starts — five runs back — gives him a foundation to build on; our ratings rank him second of 18 in the field, yet winless in recent starts and a current run of poor finishes make him a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Chica Guerrera
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with Mark Fahey, ridden by a 7lb claimer, has a solid profile at 10f on Good ground with a win and two places in her last three; steps up to 1m4f for the first time which is the key question.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 15 of 18 on our figures, Chica Guerrera faces a stiff ask, though she does arrive off a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going before; 41 days off the track and 133 lb on her back make her hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Port Of Spain
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's three-year-old wore a hood last time and bumped from an OR of 102; has course experience and a placing at 9f on Good but the step to 1m4f is untested and the 44-day break adds a further query.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Port Of Spain does at least have going experience to call on and was third four starts back, though a return from 44 days off and 131 lb to carry make further progress hard to guarantee.

runners_data.name: The Real Screamer
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's progressive five-year-old has won his last two, both at trips shorter than today's 1m4f, which is a stamina question; Luke McAteer rides and the trainer is in good form (T14: 3/19).|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, The Real Screamer faces a stiff task, though he arrives in decent nick — third last time out and a winner two and three starts back — and has experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Fixation
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh sends out this four-year-old with Ben Coen aboard; won last time over 10f on Good and has placed at 8f on similar surfaces — a prominent runner whose recent winning form is highly relevant if 1m4f suits.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 18 on our figures and carrying 130 lb, Fixation is hard to fancy despite winning last time out; the trainer's current 4% strike rate — one win from 24 in the last 14 days — adds little encouragement, though he has going experience in his favour.

runners_data.name: Touch The Moon
runners_data.note: Won over 16f and placed at 12f in recent starts, so the trip here at 1m4f represents a drop in distance for William Durkan's five-year-old; should stay well and Chris Hayes is a savvy judge of pace at Galway.|
runners_data.comment: Touch The Moon won three starts back and was runner-up two starts back, but has drifted to fourth last time out; he has distance and going experience in his favour, though carrying 130 lb could prove the key test here.

runners_data.name: Kingstonian
runners_data.note: 68 days since last run is the notable flag for Joseph O'Brien's four-year-old; wore headgear last time, placed at 2m2f and 1m6f on Good, so the stamina is assured over this shorter 1m4f trip.|
runners_data.comment: Kingstonian showed smart form when second and third in consecutive starts, but a ninth-place finish last time out raises questions, and 68 days off the track adds an element of doubt; has run over today's trip and going, though his 129 lb burden is no help.

runners_data.name: Mo Ghille Mar
runners_data.note: Won over 17f on Good, so pace and stamina are strengths for John Joseph Hanlon's five-year-old; a true hold-up horse who needs the race to be genuinely run to have a chance, and the 29-day turnaround is positive.|
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back but sixth last time out, Mo Ghille Mar has distance and going experience in her favour and 29 days off could have her fresh; however, her trainer is badly out of form at 1/21 recently, and a mark of 88 makes life tough off 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Tribal Star
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness's five-year-old is a front-runner by nature carrying a headgear flag, but with more prominent horses than positions available it will likely be taken back into midfield against its best racing style; recent form (443902) underwhelms.|
runners_data.comment: Tribal Star is winless in his last six starts but has placed second most recently and third four starts back, showing he's capable of hitting the frame; he has experience over today's trip and conditions, yet consistency remains the concern from a 128 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Mr Vettori
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides this three-year-old for Jessica Harrington, 69 days off the track and headgear-flagged; won over 8f and placed at 10f on Good, so today's 1m4f is a step into the unknown but the handler targets these spots well.|

runners_data.name: Thread Of Gold
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins's three-year-old has two wins from four starts and has only raced on Good ground, making every run directly relevant; the 22-day freshness is ideal and WJ Lee is a strong booking at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Thread Of Gold won last time out and was seventh three starts back, and that inconsistency in form makes him hard to fancy ranked 13 of 18 on our figures; going experience counts in his favour, though.

runners_data.name: Immutable
runners_data.note: Joseph Murphy's six-year-old returns from 89 days off — the longest absence in the field — and has a solitary placing on Good ground in 15 relevant runs; his natural front-running tendencies cannot be expressed in this congested pace scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 89 days off, Immutable does have distance and going experience to call on, and our rating of 97 suggests he holds more ability than his official mark of 85 implies — though that layoff may blunt his chance on reappearance.

runners_data.name: Navy Waters
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has placed at 12f and 16f on Good for Willie McCreery, but with several others wanting the same prominent berths this five-year-old is unlikely to settle where its form is built; 33-day freshness is fine.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, though a third three starts back offers a crumb of encouragement; Navy Waters has distance and going experience to call on, but carrying 125 lb off a mark of 85 makes her task no easier after 33 days off.

runners_data.name: Night Moon
runners_data.note: Mullins's six-year-old won 49 days ago over 1m6f on Good and is a genuine hold-up horse pushed into a mid-division map position; the style displacement is a mild concern, but the strong Good-ground winning form and course/distance profile keep it firmly in the picture.|
runners_data.comment: Night Moon has won two of his last four starts and arrives here having run over today's trip and going, but ranked bottom of 18 on our figures, he faces a stiff ask against this field despite his recent winning form.

runners_data.name: Satono Chevalier
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old in fine form (311813) for MK Flannery, ridden by a 3lb claimer; a natural prominent-racer who will find position difficult to secure in this traffic, though the consistent winning record at various trips on Good suggests raw ability is not in doubt.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom two on our figures and that speed rating of 69 makes him hard to fancy, though he does bring distance-and-going experience plus a third last time out; the gelding has shown winning form in recent starts but is up against it here.

runners_data.name: Narlita
runners_data.note: Siobhan Rutledge takes the ride on Henry Rogers's seven-year-old; wears headgear and has not won on Good ground in 15 attempts — an honest performer but one whose natural prominent style will be compromised by the crowded pace scenario and whose form profile at this trip is modest.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Narlita did show a flash of form with a third three starts back, yet a sixth two starts back and a fourth last time out — 41 days ago — suggest she remains frustratingly inconsistent; she has run over today's trip and going, but her rating edge may not be enough to bridge the gap.

races.paceDynamic: This Songisforyou is the confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a field of 18 at 1m4f on Good ground at Galway, the early tempo should be controlled and sustainable rather than pressured. From the gates, This Songisforyou is expected to stride into a clear lead, setting an honest but manageable gallop that gives prominent horses a relatively comfortable berth in the first half-mile. The race should develop into a genuine stamina test in the straight, where the modest early tempo rewards horses travelling well within themselves before the turn for home — a shape that classically suits prominent-to-midfield runners with a strong cruising speed over this trip rather than deep closers. This field holds significantly more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate up front — Tribal Star, Navy Waters, Immutable, Satono Chevalier and Narlita all want to race prominently but will be shuffled back into midfield against their nature, meaning the horses who do secure the prominent positions behind This Songisforyou will hold a material positional advantage; true hold-up horses coming from the rear will face a stern test unless the pace quickens appreciably.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If This Songisforyou dictates a steady gallop and horses tracking close to the pace get the first run in the straight.
scenarios.body: This Songisforyou sets an uncontested, measured tempo that compresses the field and leaves genuine closers with little ground to make up — the horses travelling second to fifth at halfway are perfectly placed to pounce when the pace lifts. Prominent types who secure a comfortable position behind the leader — and have the stamina for 1m4f on Good — are handed a decisive advantage by the race shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace produces a wall of horses turning in and one or two midfield runners produce a sustained finish to pick off the leaders.
scenarios.body: A compressed field running at a moderate gallop means the straight fills quickly, but a horse with a genuine engine travelling strongly in mid-division can thread through tiring rivals as they spread across the track. The Good ground at Galway's undulating home straight amplifies stamina questions for those who raced too close, giving a well-organised midfield horse its best chance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If This Songisforyou converts its uncontested lead into a wire-to-wire success by rationing effort perfectly and none of the chasers produce the necessary acceleration.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to challenge for the lead in the early stages, This Songisforyou can effectively dictate every fraction, and on Good ground over 1m4f a well-rated front-runner can simply stay far enough ahead that the energy cost of reeling it in exceeds what the closers have left. Emmet Mullins's runner carries a STYLE_FIT caveat racing outside its natural role here, but the lack of pace opposition is a genuine mitigating factor.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace somehow collapses or accelerates sharply mid-race, creating a truly searching gallop that drops the prominent horses and leaves the race to genuine hold-up types finishing hardest.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires something materially different from the anticipated pace picture — a break in rhythm, a fast injection at the half-way point, or leaders stopping quickly — to generate the ground-making opportunity deep closers need. Many of the nominally hold-up horses in this field are redistributed prominent types rather than true sit-and-finish horses, so this shape is the hardest to engineer and the least likely to produce a genuine closer winner.

watchPoints.text: This Songisforyou leads alone from the front — if Ronan Whelan can control fractions entirely unchallenged through the first mile, he becomes the most dangerous horse in the race regardless of STYLE_FIT concerns.

Thread Of Gold and Fixation are the two horses whose recent Good-ground winning form, correct trip, and likely race positions most directly align with the anticipated pace shape — monitor both from halfway.

Tribal Star, Navy Waters, Immutable, Satono Chevalier and Narlita all want to race prominently; a congested early break with 18 runners could cause interference or force genuine front-runners sideways — watch the first two furlongs closely.
Kingstonian and Mr Vettori both return from 68+ days off the track with headgear flags — if either is not fully wound up, their price may misrepresent their readiness rather than their ability.

Touch The Moon drops significantly in trip from recent wins over 16f — if the pace is steady and the stamina test is diluted, this runner may lack the gears to compete; a strongly-run race over today's shorter trip would suit it far more.

races.name: Arthur Guinness Handicap

runners_data.name: Casamorati
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer for O'Brien whose recent form string of 6-8-9-8 on Good ground shows consistent failure to land a blow; fades in the finish and with no ability to access a prominent position in this field, the midfield shuffle makes a winning chance very remote.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Casamorati has experience over today's trip and conditions, yet his recent run of eighth, ninth and eighth tells against him; at 140 lb from stall 3, he'll need a career-best to get involved from fifth in our ratings.

runners_data.name: Only One Scobie
runners_data.note: Recorded a win at Healey and showed a placed effort over 7f on Soft but three subsequent double-figure finishes on Good are alarming; hold-up style and fade flag make this field structure deeply unkind, and Flynn's yard is modestly fired at T14.
runners_data.comment: Returned unplaced last time but was third two starts back and a winner three starts back, giving his recent form a mixed look; he has run over today's distance and going before, though 140 lb from stall 16 are factors to weigh against him.

runners_data.name: Sweet Baby Zou
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good and has tried this sort of trip before, but hasn't run for 56 days and her hold-up style with a fade flag leaves her vulnerable to the midfield congestion; the return from a near-two-month absence is the key unknown.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back but unplaced last time out, and 56 days off adds a fitness query; she has experience of today's trip and going, though her speed rating of 63 leaves her with plenty to find against the top-rated runners from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Femme Beauty
runners_data.note: Legitimate prominent-racing filly with two wins on Good ground and a habit of performing at around 10-12f; OR=69 is competitive, O'Leary stable is quiet at T14 but she is one of the few runners here whose natural race position actually matches the map, making her structurally well-placed.
runners_data.comment: Femme Beauty won last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, but a 39-day absence and a stiff 139 lb from stall 19 are real tests of whether she can back that up at this level.

runners_data.name: Good Man Jack
runners_data.note: Three career runs, all modest finishes on Good ground, with a fade-in-finish flag and hold-up style; Magee yard is cold at T14 and there is nothing in the form to suggest this wide-open handicap presents a real opportunity.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a seventh and ninth among recent efforts, Good Man Jack arrives here ranked last on our figures and carrying 139 lb from stall 18 — he has run over today's trip and going before, but there is precious little in the form to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Hassaniya
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner; has placed in two of her last five including a third over 12f on Good, and the tongue-tie and pace-cloth combination suggest O'Callaghan is trying to activate her best form at the front — the key is whether the tempo is sustainable enough to steal it.
runners_data.comment: Hassaniya has been knocking on the door with back-to-back thirds in recent starts, and he has experience over today's distance and going. Carrying 139 lb from stall 20, our rating of 85 marks him as the one to beat, though he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: In The Gloaming
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose headgear (p) was added recently, with form of 5-5-6-12 over sprint to 7f trips suggesting this 1m½f trip is a significant step up; Carroll is a capable jockey but the distance query and backmarker position are both negatives.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, In The Gloaming has at least shown consistency with consecutive fifth-place finishes, and has run over today's going before; the 139 lb burden from stall 15 makes life harder for a gelding yet to find the winner's enclosure.

runners_data.name: Down The Glen
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Heavy and placed at 8f on Soft, so his best form has come on softer surfaces; Good going today is less ideal and his hold-up style means he needs traffic to part — hasn't run for 57 days which adds further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Down The Glen showed smart form when winning earlier in the sequence and has experience of today's distance and going, while our rating of 77 ranks him second of 21 runners — a strong threat. The main risk is a 57-day absence combined with an unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Mr Perth
runners_data.note: Unraced style tag (U) with a fade flag, and three runs all finishing in the bottom half on varied going; 77 days off and no notable positives from trainer or jockey angle — difficult to make a case here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked 17th of 21 on our figures, Mr Perth faces a stiff task here; 77 days off the track raises freshness doubts, though he has run over today's trip and going before and stall six is a neutral draw.

runners_data.name: Tharaka
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse that has been mapped into midfield through redistribution because the backmarker slots are oversubscribed; Mullins-trained and returning after 305 days off, the lengthy absence is a serious concern, and racing out of its natural position (STYLE_FIT=0.92) reduces its chance materially.
runners_data.comment: Twice a fourth and placed third in recent starts, Tharaka has run over today's trip and going and her rating of 76 marks her as a serious player from stall 12 — the concern is 305 days off the track leaves her fitness an open question.

runners_data.name: Belle Nuit
runners_data.note: Hold-up type shifted into the midfield map through redistribution, having raced only four times with a best of 4th over 7f on Soft; Nolan yard is quiet at T14, and being unable to access its preferred deep position (STYLE_FIT=0.90) diminishes an already modest profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Belle Nuit does bring going experience to the table and 23 days between runs leaves her reasonably fresh; however, consecutive unplaced efforts head into this, and carrying 135 lb from stall 2 makes the task no easier.

runners_data.name: Aquilla Star
runners_data.note: Placed twice — second over 10f on Good and second over 7f on Heavy — so has some ability, but is a true hold-up horse compressed into midfield by redistribution (STYLE_FIT=0.92); back quickly after 11 days, and the headgear (p) is retained.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 15th of 21 on our figures, Aquilla Star faces a stiff ask, with her trainer yet to land a winner in 22 attempts over the past fortnight; experience over today's going is the one gentle positive.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Funk
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing type with headgear and six runs showing consistent mid-pack finishes; second over 8f on Heavy is the best result, and while the prominent style is an asset in this race shape, the form ceiling looks limited against these rivals at OR=64.
runners_data.comment: Cosmic Funk ran a solid second three starts back and returns here on a retrieval mission just 16 days later, with experience of both today's trip and going working in his favour — the main concern is that he's been winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: John La Bear
runners_data.note: Won over 8f at Standside last year but that was on a different surface profile; returned 7th on Good most recently after 30 days off, and though a true hold-up type mapped to midfield through redistribution (STYLE_FIT=0.92), the tongue-tie is retained and Ross O'Sullivan's yard is quiet.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back but has been below that level since, and with a speed rating of 54 he faces a stiff ask against 20 rivals; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, though 134 lb from stall 8 is no easy proposition.

runners_data.name: Jp's Express
runners_data.note: Placed once over 8f on Good in six career starts and carries headgear (p); a genuine hold-up horse that cannot reach its natural position due to redistribution (STYLE_FIT=0.90), and Joyce claims 3lb which may help marginally, but the structural disadvantage is real.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with two unplaced efforts among them, Jp's Express is hard to fancy on these figures — ranked 18 of 21 in the field. A return to form third last time out offers slim encouragement, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Snaafy
runners_data.note: Useful form profile — won over 8f on Standside and placed multiple times — and Loughnane is a competitive handler; though a true hold-up type mapped to midfield (STYLE_FIT=0.92), Snaafy has the most compelling underlying form of the redistributed group and McDonogh adds significant jockey quality.
runners_data.comment: Snaafy hasn't won in his last four starts, and ranked 20 of 21 on our figures he faces a stiff task here; second last time out offers a crumb of comfort, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but the weight of 134 lb doesn't help his cause.

runners_data.name: Aurora Mist
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden by Andrew Slattery which is unusual; won over 8f on Good and placed at 7f on Heavy, showing some versatility, but is a hold-up horse placed in midfield by redistribution (STYLE_FIT=0.91) and the tongue-tie suggests she needs managing carefully.
runners_data.comment: Aurora Mist won two starts back but has been unplaced on her most recent outing, and ranked 16th of 21 on our figures she faces a stiff ask here; the experience over today's trip and going, plus a 16-day turnaround, at least count in her favour.

runners_data.name: Love Orchid
runners_data.note: Unraced style tag (U) with blinkers, five runs all in the 4th-9th range on Good; Meade's yard has three from 13 at T14 which is respectable but there is little in the form to project a step forward here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Love Orchid nevertheless drops a shade in class on our rating and has run over today's trip and going before; the 133 lb burden from stall 13 is the chief concern for a filly who has yet to threaten the frame in recent outings.

runners_data.name: Priorstown
runners_data.note: Three career runs, best of 6th over 8f on Heavy; hold-up type redistributed to midfield (STYLE_FIT=0.90) and returns from 84 days off — the long layoff combined with the structural disadvantage makes this a very difficult winning case.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and returning after 84 days off, Priorstown has experience of today's distance and going but his trainer is struggling badly at 1/24 over the past fortnight, which tempers any claims despite our rating of 72 suggesting he holds a little more ability than his official mark implies.

runners_data.name: Ella's Gold
runners_data.note: Five placed efforts without winning but has run into form on Good ground over 9-10f; prominent-racing type with headgear (p) who has a legitimate claim to sit close to the pace in a race where that position is genuinely scarce — one of the few who can access the right spot naturally.
runners_data.comment: Ella's Gold has shown consistent placing ability, finishing second three times and third once in her last five starts, though she remains yet to win in recent form. She has run over today's trip and going before, and 31 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Dont Get Me Wrong
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standside and has shown some consistency, but is a true hold-up horse compressed into midfield through redistribution (STYLE_FIT=0.92); returns after 31 days without a jockey booking visible, and the redistribution penalty is a meaningful handicap in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 19 of 21 on our figures, Dont Get Me Wrong has been out of the frame in his last three starts — seventh, ninth, and eighth — and it's hard to look past that slump despite him having run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Hassaniya is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 21-runner handicap over 1m½f at Galway and, crucially, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without being pressured into burning her reserves. With only Femme Beauty, Cosmic Funk, and Ella's Gold as mapped prominent types, the early-to-mid sections of this race should be orderly rather than frenetic, creating a genuine advantage for anything travelling sweetly in the first three to five positions. The overwhelming majority of this field are hold-up types, but the REDISTRIBUTED flags on Tharaka, Belle Nuit, Snaafy, Aquilla Star, John La Bear, Jp's Express, Aurora Mist, Priorstown, and Dont Get Me Wrong confirm that many true hold-up horses cannot secure their natural backmarker position — they will be shuffled into a congested midfield, blunted by traffic and unable to produce their best late challenge. This race shape — one uncontested leader, a thin front group, and a bulging, fractured midfield — firmly favours horses racing prominently or in the first half-dozen, able to travel on the pace and pick off a front-runner who has had it too easy, rather than late closers fighting through a wall of horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hassaniya Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Hassaniya bowls along uncontested and sets a fair-to-modest tempo, a prominent tracker pounces in the straight.
scenarios.body: Hassaniya's uncontested lead allows her to conserve energy through the race, but a sustainable pace means a well-placed prominent racer travelling just behind her can reel her in without needing to make extreme ground. Femme Beauty and Cosmic Funk, both legitimate prominent types with decent recent records on Good, are best positioned to strike as the front-runner ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hassaniya Front-Runs Wire to Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely modest and no prominent racer has the class to close, Hassaniya steals it from the front.
scenarios.body: A single uncontested front-runner setting a sedate pace over 1m½f on Good ground is the classic front-runner's paradise, and Hassaniya's recent form shows she has placed on similar trips in similar conditions. No horse in this field has the confirmed acceleration to run her down if she has built a cushion mid-race and is not pressured.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Congested Midfield, One Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up horses create a genuine traffic logjam in the straight, one runner finds a gap and surges late.
scenarios.body: With nine runners compressed into midfield through redistribution, the straight at Galway will be crowded, but the rare horse that finds a clear passage — Snaafy or Aquilla Star, who have at least shown ability to place — could benefit from rivals checking each other. This is a lower-probability shape because so many of the natural closers are racing out of role and their STYLE_FIT penalties reduce the likelihood of a clean, decisive late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Group Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is misjudged and Hassaniya sets a stronger gallop than expected, a hold-up type benefits from a genuine finishing opportunity.
scenarios.body: A stronger pace would theoretically open the door for backmarkers, but the redistribution of most genuine hold-up types into midfield means few horses are truly positioned to exploit a strong pace from the rear. This scenario is the least likely given the confirmed one-pace dynamic and the structural impossibility of most closers reaching their natural deep position in a 21-runner field.

watchPoints.text: Hassaniya's early position is unchallenged — watch whether Sean Davis elects to dictate or drops her in, as any deviation from front-running immediately changes the race shape and removes the primary pace scenario.

The midfield in this 21-runner field will be extremely congested given nine redistributed hold-up types cannot access the rear — watch for significant interference and traffic issues in the straight, particularly affecting Snaafy, Tharaka, and Belle Nuit.

Femme Beauty's jockey Danny O'Leary is a 10lb claimer in a 21-runner handicap — watch for positional errors in the early stages that could negate her prominent-style advantage, which is the key structural edge she holds.

Tharaka returns after 305 days off for Emmet Mullins — watch the market move for any intelligence on whether this absence reflects a setback or a planned fresh campaign, as the form shown prior to the break suggests some latent ability.

Snaafy holds the strongest form credentials of the redistributed hold-up group (won over 8f, multiple places, Declan McDonogh aboard) — watch whether he can manoeuvre into a better-than-mapped position early, as even a mid-division berth could be enough if the front group tires.

races.name: Hop House 13 Handicap

runners_data.name: Celtic Druid
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a recent win over 12f on standard and solid handicap form; McCourt yard in T14 form (1/8) and Sadhbh Tormey's claim useful in this weight-sensitive handicap; well-suited to good ground and likely to travel fluently just off Tatum.
runners_data.comment: Celtic Druid has placed last time out and was third two starts back, but ranked 19 of 21 on our figures, he looks up against it here; the experience over today's trip and going offers some consolation, though 140 lb is a stern burden.

runners_data.name: Lady Plimsoll
runners_data.note: 123 days off the track is a notable flag, though she placed over 16f on standard and 12f on good; O'Callaghan yard sends out T14 1/8, suggesting intent; a prominent profile suits this shape but fitness after a long absence is the key unknown.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but has placed twice in that sequence and brings solid each-way claims here as the top-rated runner; she has run over today's going before, and third last time out and a second two starts back suggest she retains form, though 123 days off will need to be overcome.

runners_data.name: Tatum
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner and sole pace-setter, but tagged as racing out of role and Noel Meade's T14 form strong (3/13); likely to control fractions at a sustainable clip — a clear tactical factor for the whole field rather than a straightforward win candidate.
runners_data.comment: Tatum arrives on the back of a win last time out and a victory five starts back, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour. Carrying 140 lb after just eight days' turnaround is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Baila Conmigo
runners_data.note: Ran only yesterday (LR:1d) which is an obvious fitness/fatigue concern; prominent profile is well-suited if fresh enough, but form over 16f on good is limited and the quick turnaround must be discounted.
runners_data.comment: Baila Conmigo won last time out and has going experience in his favour, but his two wins in his last six starts are offset by a fifth two runs back, and 139 lb is a stern ask for a gelding ranked 14 of 21 on our ratings.

runners_data.name: Hexagonal
runners_data.note: Recent OR=69 winner over 10f on good but those efforts came at much shorter trips; stepping up significantly in distance to 1m6f, which his pedigree and form profile make questionable despite a good-ground profile.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win last time out, but six days is a quick turnaround and he's been inconsistent in recent starts, with four finishes outside the placings in his last six. Has run over today's going, and 139 lb is no featherweight.

runners_data.name: Steps In The Sand
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong good-ground form over staying trips including 13/15 wins from similar going; Ciaran Murphy yard also sends Baila Conmigo, suggesting stable interest; at 7yo consistent at this level and the trip suits well.
runners_data.comment: Steps In The Sand showed she could compete when second four starts back and a winner five starts back, but three consecutive unplaced efforts since tell against her. She has experience over today's trip and going, and 19 days since her last run suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Goin'
runners_data.note: W J Lee takes the ride for A J Martin (1/6 T14) on a hold-up performer who stays well over 16-19f on good; form figures suggest mid-pack finishes rather than wins but this pace shape and trip combination is exactly where he's competitive.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and third four starts back, Goin' has shown consistency without a win in his last five starts, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the 138 lb burden is the key concern for a gelding operating off a mark of 68.

runners_data.name: Trubshaw
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's team strong in T14 (6/42) and the horse carries a headgear-p flag; though shown in midfield on the map, this is a genuinely prominent horse pushed back by field size — his best form includes a win over 14f on good and he is capable of getting into contention if he can secure a forward position.
runners_data.comment: Trubshaw won four starts back but has finished sixth, unplaced, and eighth in his last three, making recent form the concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and an eight-day turnaround keeps him fresh, though 138 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Cooley's Mist
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 13f on good with multiple placings at this level; a horse who wants to race prominently but has been redistributed to midfield given the field's makeup — if he can assert closer to the front than the map shows, his form makes him a live player.
runners_data.comment: Cooley's Mist arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's distance and going, yet he sits mid-pack on ratings and carries 136 lb, which may blunt his recent momentum.

runners_data.name: Mr Rango
runners_data.note: 10yo with a place over 17f on good and consistent middle-to-rear finishes; trainer has no T14 runners and no jockey listed, limiting confidence; a hold-up profile over this trip on good ground is workable but win record is poor.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six, Mr Rango nonetheless showed real quality when second two starts back, and a rating of 74 among a 21-runner field marks him as a leading threat; the risk is that last-time-out ninth leaves his consistency open to question.

runners_data.name: Quiz Test
runners_data.note: Shane Foley aboard a genuine prominent-profile horse forced into a midfield role by the sheer volume of front-runners; best form has come over 14-17f on good; best watched to see if Foley can manoeuvre forward — style-fit discount applies given forced position.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts, Quiz Test at least brings distance and going experience to the table, and a speed rating of 76 hints at ability — though 51 days off and a hefty 136 lb burden are the key questions to answer here.

runners_data.name: Blackjack Hills
runners_data.note: Ran only yesterday (LR:1d), holds blinkers, and is a hold-up type from a distance profile that is shorter than today's 1m6f; the quick turnaround and step up in trip are dual concerns, though Robbie Colgan is a capable handler in competitive handicaps.
runners_data.comment: Backed up a recent second with a win three starts back, but ranked 20 of 21 on our figures and a seventh two starts back undermines confidence; going experience at least gives him a foothold.

runners_data.name: Coulstys Way
runners_data.note: Four-year-old prominent racer whose best form is over 14f on good; the redistribution to midfield reflects the overcrowded prominent ranks — Patrick Magee has no T14 winners and the horse's form figures suggest inconsistency, limiting appeal.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 15th of 21 on our figures, Coulstys Way faces a stiff task here; third last time out and a second four starts back offer faint encouragement, and she has run over today's trip and going before, returning on a fresh 16 days.

runners_data.name: Nancee Spain
runners_data.note: Fresh after 35 days off; hold-up profile with a win on soft and placed on good over 12f; the step up to 1m6f looks a positive, and Scott McCullagh's claim is useful — the blinkers flag adds a headgear variable worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Nancee Spain has run over today's trip and going, and a win four starts back shows she can find the line — but her last three runs have all been out of the frame, and that dip in form is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Bell Ex Too
runners_data.note: Three-year-old at OR=70 racing against older horses; only four career runs, all resulting in mid-pack finishes; the distance of 1m6f is a significant step up and the experience deficit in a 21-runner handicap is a real concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Bell Ex Too arrives 20 days fresh and has run over today's going before, but a string of mid-pack finishes — sixth, seventh, fifth, sixth — and a speed rating of 60 suggest he faces a stiff task off 129 lb against a field of 21.

runners_data.name: Vantage Code
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes a 3yo with a headgear-h flag; placed on good ground over 12f and showed ability at 10f; the step to 1m6f is an unknown but Emmet Mullins (T14 1/11) is capable and Coen is among the sharper jockey bookings in this field.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and second two starts back, Vantage Code shows consistent placing ability in recent starts, though winless in his last five and a return just four days ago raises freshness questions; has run over today's going, and 128 lb is workable at this level.

runners_data.name: Blissful Bonita
runners_data.note: Three-year-old by Gary Carroll for Gavin Cromwell (T14 1/37); a horse whose natural front-running profile means she would want to be prominent but the field size makes that impossible — Carroll will need to balance position against energy in what looks a tough assignment.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with finishes no better than second in that spell and a trainer currently in the depths of a lean spell (1 from 35 in the past fortnight), Blissful Bonita — ranked 17th of 21 on our figures — faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Espritroyale
runners_data.note: Cromwell's second runner in this race; hold-up profile stepping up to 1m6f having raced over 6-10f; very limited experience at this trip and the form figures on good ground are modest — placed last time over 10f on soft but this is a big ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 18th of 21 on our figures, Espritroyale faces a stiff task, with the trainer in poor nick at 1/35 over the past fortnight; second last time out is the one genuine positive to cling to.

runners_data.name: Lauro's Legend
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a serious concern over 1m6f in a competitive handicap; recent form reads 700 and the going report does not ameliorate the finishing concern; best treated with caution regardless of early positioning.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked 16th of 21 on our figures, Lauro's Legend has little recent form to recommend him despite experience over today's trip and going; the 134 lb burden adds further pressure on a gelding who needs to rediscover his best.

runners_data.name: Out On Friday
runners_data.note: 10yo hold-up type whose best recent result was 2nd over 10f on good; redistributed from a rear position to midfield but naturally wants to come from off the pace; Philip Byrne's yard has only 1 runner in T14 and no jockey listed — hard to weigh up with confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, though he did post a second three starts back to show he's capable of mixing it; seventh last time out, 15 days ago, keeps him relatively fresh, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Covert Legend
runners_data.note: Consistent placer who has finished 4th four times in recent starts without winning; hold-up profile with good-ground form over 11-12f; stepping up in trip to 1m6f and Maurice Ahern has no T14 runners — the horse's profile suggests a likely finisher rather than winner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with four fourths and a second three starts back, Covert Legend faces a stiff task here — ranked last on our figures, though he has experience of today's going and returns after a 27-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Tatum is the confirmed sole front-runner in this 21-runner 1m6f handicap and, crucially, is tagged as racing out of role at OR=70 — meaning the pace on offer is likely to be sustainable and unhurried rather than pressured or fierce. With only one genuine pace-setter among a field dominated by prominent and hold-up types, the early fractions should be controlled, setting up a race that will be decided by those who can travel well just off the leader and produce a sustained finish rather than a late burst. The redistributed prominent types — Trubshaw, Quiz Test, Cooley's Mist, Coulstys Way and Blissful Bonita — are genuine front-to-midfield horses who cannot all secure their natural position in a field this large, meaning the area just behind the leader will be compressed and competitive. This race shape strongly favours horses with genuine prominent-to-midfield profiles who can travel within themselves on a gentle pace and then sustain their effort over the final three furlongs — front-runners and those who settle in the first half dozen runners are best placed, while true hold-up types will need exceptional finishing runs from well off the pace in a field unlikely to fall apart.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tatum Dictates, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Tatum sets a controlled, uncontested pace and horses racing prominently just behind can travel and quicken in the straight.
scenarios.body: Tatum's lead is sustainable rather than scorching, rewarding those who sit two to five lengths off and stay balanced around Galway's undulations; when the tempo lifts in the final quarter-mile the horses with the clearest passage and best finishing kick from a prominent berth will dominate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is so sedate that a wall of horses hits the front simultaneously, allowing hold-up runners to produce late momentum.
scenarios.body: A pedestrian first mile would compress the field, making it a sprint finish in which hold-up runners who have saved energy can produce strong late runs; Galway's finish does reward sustained galloping, not pure sprinting, but an unusually slow pace could offset that.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens Mid-Race, Stayers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Tatum is pressed sooner than expected and the race develops into a genuine test of stamina from halfway.
scenarios.body: A stronger pace than anticipated will string the field out and eliminate the one-paced prominent types, rewarding those who stay on relentlessly up the straight; at 1m6f on good ground this shape suits genuine stayers with positive recent form at the trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Large Field, Outsider Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If traffic issues, positional battles and uneven pacing create pockets of clear air for a hold-up runner from further back than ideal.
scenarios.body: With 21 runners the midfield will be congested and gaps hard to find, but a horse that finds a clear run at the right moment could benefit from rivals being checked or hampered; this scenario favours lightly-raced or fresh horses in good form who have the pace to capitalise when daylight appears.

watchPoints.text: Tatum holds the race's only genuine pace and is racing out of role — if she fails to stride on from the gates or is immediately challenged, the field will bunch badly entering the far side and create chaos for all 21 runners.

Baila Conmigo and Blackjack Hills both ran yesterday (LR:1d) and are prominent-profile runners; fatigue in either could cause them to drop away sharply mid-race and impede horses tracking behind them.

The volume of redistributed prominent types — Trubshaw, Cooley's Mist, Quiz Test, Coulstys Way and Blissful Bonita — means an early scramble for position is likely in the first two furlongs; watch for crowding on the rail and interference in the first half-mile.

Lauro's Legend is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish and recent form reads 700 — with 21 runners, a fading horse from mid-to-rear could compromise the runs of those attempting late surges behind it.

Ben Coen on Vantage Code and Shane Foley on Quiz Test are the two most notable jockey bookings for horses carrying style-fit or redistribution caveats — watch whether either can manoeuvre into a more natural position in the early stages, as that would significantly enhance their chances.

races.name: Rockshore Refreshingly Irish Race

runners_data.name: Counting Coup
runners_data.note: Ran a fair race over 12f on Good ground in latest start but is a natural front-runner or prominent racer who figures to find this trip and a field containing Uxmal working against securing his preferred forward position; at 31 days between runs he arrives relatively fresh but his form figures of 14 over similar trips are limited.
runners_data.comment: Counting Coup arrives here a winner two starts back and goes on today's going, giving him plenty to work with off 135 lb; the main risk is that his most recent start since that victory ended in a fourth, suggesting he can be inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Taipan
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes the ride for Mrs Harrington, and Taipan's sole win at the 1m4f trip on Good ground is his most relevant piece of positive form; 89 days off the track is notable, and his recent history over shorter, heavier-ground trips is largely disappointing, though he is not without ability if conditions click.
runners_data.comment: Taipan showed he can win at this level with a victory five starts back, and he has distance and going experience to call on carrying 135 lb; the chief concern is whether he returns to peak form after 89 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Teed Up
runners_data.note: Carries a fade-in-finish flag and is a genuine hold-up horse by nature, though the map places him in midfield because there are simply more hold-up runners than the race shape can absorb at the back; Mullins sends him out just four days after his last run, and his best recent effort was a third at 17f on Good ground suggesting the distance suits, but the finishing weakness is a real concern.
runners_data.comment: Teed Up has run over today's trip and going before, but one unplaced effort in his last three starts makes him hard to fancy, and he ranks fifth of six on our figures — though a win four starts back and back-to-back thirds suggest he retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Uxmal
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter and class horse of the race at OR=105, Joseph O'Brien's runner has wins over a range of trips including 1m10f on Good and 1m14f on Soft; he carries 131lbs and his rider Sheridan takes the mount from a yard firing at 15/68 over 14 days, making this an intended competitive run rather than a school.
runners_data.comment: Uxmal showed his class with a win four starts back and returned to form with a third last time out, and he has experience of today's trip and going. Carrying 131 lb is the one test, but on his best he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Way Down South
runners_data.note: Gillian Scott's hold-up specialist has a quietly consistent record staying on for places at this distance on Good ground, including a second at 22f and a third at 19f; only 11 days since his last run, he arrives with fitness but his trainer has a blank 14-day record (0/3) and he has yet to win in recent form figures of 957.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a seventh last time out and a fifth two starts back, Way Down South looks up against it here — our rating places him last of six in the field, though 11 days since his latest run at least suggests freshness, and he has experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Galileo Dame
runners_data.note: The five-year-old from O'Brien's yard carries the 7lb claimer Pietropaolo and is a prominent-racing type who should track Uxmal throughout; four days between runs is quick, and his form figures of -24770 show recency without wins, though a second at 14f on Heavy suggests he stays well and can match strides with the leader.

races.paceDynamic: Uxmal is the confirmed front-runner and, in a six-runner field over 1m6f on Good ground, will stride to the front from the outset and control tempo without serious challenge. The pace he sets is likely to be honest rather than frenetic — a measured, sustainable gallop that suits his profile and keeps the race together through the early stages. Counting Coup and Galileo Dame are the two most likely rivals to press him for a prominent pitch, with Teed Up and Way Down South expected to settle further back in a hold-up berth. This shape — one leader controlling from the front on a fair surface — strongly favours the prominent-to-front profile: any horse close to the pace will have first run into the home straight and avoid being caught in traffic. The field holds more prominent types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate; Counting Coup and Galileo Dame will contest that second/third position, and one of them is likely to be shuffled back against their preference, most probably Counting Coup given his redistribution flag.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uxmal Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Uxmal dictates a fair tempo and the field is unable to close him down turning for home.
scenarios.body: Uxmal leads throughout at a sensible gallop on Good ground, and with no genuine front-runner to apply pressure, he simply finds his rhythm and stays on strongly to the line; his OR=105 is the class benchmark in this company. Horses close to him throughout, particularly Galileo Dame, are the primary threats to pick up the pieces if he weakens late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Galileo Dame tracks Uxmal tightly throughout and outstays him in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Uxmal's pace draws Galileo Dame into a perfect position, and the younger horse — carrying 126lbs and trained by a yard in excellent form — uses that lead-off energy to hit the front approaching the last furlong. Uxmal's jumping history (hg:p) and possible tiredness at the end of a Good-ground staying test could see him capitulate to a fresher rival.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Uxmal's pace is genuinely strong and creates enough of a test that closers can reel in the leaders in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Way Down South or Taipan, settled well off the pace, find the race has been run to suit them and pick off a tiring front end; Taipan showed a course win over 14f in Good conditions and Shane Foley will have him switched off for a late challenge. However, both horses' recent form over similar trips is modest, limiting the likelihood of this unfolding.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Uxmal is challenged hard early by Counting Coup or Galileo Dame, inflating the pace and causing the field to bunch and race competitively throughout.
scenarios.body: A more pressured gallop weakens the prominent types, leaving the race open to Taipan or Way Down South rounding the home turn with momentum; this scenario depends on Counting Coup overriding redistribution and genuinely pressing Uxmal, which is not his natural game at this trip. The low probability reflects how few genuine pace disruptors this small field actually contains.

watchPoints.text: Uxmal could be left alone in front at a comfortable gallop — if he gets an uncontested lead and sets his own pace, he becomes very difficult to peg back at this OR, and any horse drawn to track him closely will need to sustain the effort all the way to the line.

Counting Coup is a natural prominent type who may attempt to press Uxmal early despite his redistribution — if he does, watch for a contested pace that could compromise both horses and open the door for closers.

Teed Up's fade-in-finish flag combined with Mullins running him just four days after his previous start is a combination to treat with caution — the horse may not be at peak readiness and his tendency to weaken late makes him vulnerable in the final stages.

Taipan's 89-day absence is the longest layoff in the field — Shane Foley's handling of him early in the race will reveal whether he is ready to produce his best, and his Good-ground win at 14f remains his most relevant positive piece of form.

Galileo Dame carries the only apprentice claim in the race (Pietropaolo 7lb) — in a small-field prominent-pace scenario, positional decisions in the home straight are critical and the claim weight offset may prove significant if race-riding experience matters down the Galway hill.
